title: Marion Delarue. Pen, Pencil, Scissors
summary: In the fall of 2026, the Museum of Decorative Arts will present Marion Delarue’s works in the Drawings, Wallpapers, and Photographs Gallery, the result of the artist’s residency at the museum. Marion Delarue draws inspiration from the world of ceremonial adornment, which is embodied through her ongoing preoccupations with the body. Her pieces, which constantly question the notion of wearability, play on the blurring of lines between authenticity and imitation, between nature and artifice, exploring the concepts of simulacrum and metamorphosis.

title: Rafael Pavarotti. Photographer
summary: For the first time in France, the Musée des Arts Décoratifs presents the work of Brazilian photographer Rafael Pavarotti from October 2, 2026, to May 2, 2027. The exhibition showcases over 200 prints, juxtaposed with photographs from the museum’s collection, from the iconic fashion magazine covers to portraits of international pop culture stars such as Rihanna, Harry Styles, and Beyoncé, as well as campaigns he has created for major fashion houses. His work is characterized by a vibrant, powerful style, producing striking and unique images. Born in 1993 in Pará, within the Amazon rainforest, Pavarotti’s personal history resonates throughout his photographic approach. Strong women in his family, the bright, colorful dishware of his grandmother, and the natural environment of his childhood are central sources of inspiration.

title: Look: 40 Years of Fashion at the Museum
summary: To celebrate the 40th anniversary of the founding of the Musée des Arts de la Mode within its walls, the Musée des Arts Décoratifs is presenting an exhibition featuring 40 iconic outfits. The major exhibition, “Look: 40 Years of Fashion at the Museum” reveals the craftsmanship and techniques of the fashion world. From sewing workshops to behind-the-scenes at the museum, these techniques transform garments into works of art. The exhibition invites visitors to follow the dual life of a garment, from before to after it enters the collections. It unveils the stages of creation, conservation, and restoration that bring this exceptional heritage to life, from the initial sketch to the runway show, via fashion photography, and from the museum’s storage to the exhibition. Visitors can discover the beauty of the works and objects that contribute to creating a fashion piece, such as drawings, embroidery samples, patterns, and model archives. Enhanced by photography and worn by increasingly famous models, garments become the stars of fashion shows, which are now conceived as true artistic performances.

title: La Mode en Majesté. Royal Thai Dress from Tradition to Modernity
summary: The Musée des Arts Décoratifs presents a unique exhibition on the clothing evolution at the Thai court, featuring pieces from the royal collection. Gathering more than a hundred exceptional garments and accessories, the exhibition showcases the royal wardrobes, highlighting the eight traditional Thai costume formats designed by Her Majesty Queen Sirikit in collaboration with a team of historians and local Thai designers. The exhibition also emphasizes the unique history of cultural and artistic dialogue, marked by over thirty years of collaboration between Queen Sirikit and fashion designer Pierre Balmain, later continued with the Balmain and Lesage houses. Organized in collaboration with the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles in Thailand and The Sustainable Arts and Crafts Institute of Thailand (SACIT), the exhibition coincides with the celebrations of the 170th and 340th anniversaries of diplomatic relations between France and Thailand (formerly the Kingdom of Siam).

title: The World of Viktor&Rolf. 30 Years of Haute Couture
summary: From January 28 through July 4, 2027, the Musée des Arts Décoratifs presents Le monde de Viktor&Rolf. 30 ans de haute couture, a major retrospective dedicated to the Dutch design duo Viktor Horsting and Rolf Snoeren. Originally conceived by the Kunsthalle München and curator Thierry-Maxime Loriot in close collaboration with the House of Viktor&Rolf, the Paris presentation traces more than three decades of work that has continually pushed the boundaries between fashion, art, and performance. Featuring more than 100 haute couture creations, the designers’ iconic miniature dolls, archival materials, and immersive installations, the exhibition invites visitors into the singular world of Viktor&Rolf. It highlights a creative practice that seamlessly combines exceptional craftsmanship, theatricality, and conceptual innovation

title: A Day in the Eighteenth Century: Chronicle of a Parisian Townhouse
summary: The Musée des Arts Décoratifs invites visitors to step inside the intimate world of an eighteenth-century aristocratic residence and its inhabitants – masters, servants, and household animals. Featuring more than 550 original objects, drawn from the museum’s collections and for most of them, rarely exhibited, ’A Day in the Eighteenth Century: Chronicle of a Parisian Townhouse’ gather all fields of expression of the decorative arts – wood panelling and wallpapers, furniture, ceramics, silverware, clothing and fashion accessories, toys, and jewellery – to recreate the life of a Parisian hôtel particulier in the 1780s. In a cinematic, sound-filled and scented atmosphere, the visitors wander from room to room as if they were close acquaintances, friends, or privileged guests of the family.

title: The language of Walls: Rubbings from China to Notre-Dame
summary: From March 18 to June 28, 2026, the Musée des Arts Décoratifs presents Le langage des murs. Estampages de la Chine à Notre-Dame, the fourth focus exhibition in the Drawing, Wallpaper and Photography Department, coinciding with the Salon du Dessin and Printemps Asiatique. Featuring around one hundred works—including ancient and contemporary rubbings, drawings, and technical tools—the exhibition showcases the art of stone rubbing through a unique selection of the museum’s Chinese and French collections. On that occasion, the museum invites Santiago Hardy, a steepljack, and Delphine Syvilay, then research engineer at the Laboratory for Research on Historic Monuments (LRMH), to present for the first time the marks of the stonemasons and the stamped graffiti uncovered during the restoration of Notre-Dame de Paris.

title: 1925-2025. One Hundred Years of Art Deco
summary: The Musée des Arts Décoratifs celebrates the centenary of Art Deco with an exhibition of contemporary scenography. In 1925, the International Exhibition of Modern Decorative and Industrial Arts in Paris marked the peak of Art Deco. Decorators, manufacturers, magazines, department stores, artists, and even foreign nations competed fiercely to occupy Parisian buildings or erect temporary structures to display their latest creations. From October 22, 2025, to April 26, 2026, the Musée des Arts Décoratifs will celebrate the centenary of this great style and its success with an exhibition of contemporary scenography.
